title: Annular, longitudinal and spiral wall thickenings of plant cells are cylinder geodetics

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Annular, longitudinal and spiral wall thickenings of plant cells are cylinder geodetics

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The three kinds of geodetic on a cylinder (parallel rings, straight longitudinal lines and helical spirals) are all realised in the local wall thickenings of cylindrical plant cells and vessels, and the helical geodetic in the spiral coils of insect tracheae and tracheids.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: geodesics on a cylinder of radius r: circles z = c, lines \theta = c, helices z = a\theta

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: A Parenthetic Note on Geodetics

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: These three systems are all of frequent occurrence, and are all illustrated in the local thickenings of the wall of the cylindrical cells or vessels of plants.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter X, “A Parenthetic Note on Geodetics”; topic “Geodetics of the cylinder”. Scope: plant xylem vessels and tracheids, insect tracheae

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: geodesics on a cylinder of radius r: circles z = c, lines \theta = c, helices z = a\theta

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch10-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometric criterion is explicit and standard image analysis is feasible. Existing images can test representative structures, though cross-taxon coverage and deviations from cylindrical geometry limit the full generalization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit centerlines of annular, longitudinal and helical wall thickenings to geodesics on reconstructed cylindrical cell, vessel and tracheal surfaces. Support requires low geodesic curvature compared with plausible nongeodesic curves across the named structures.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Real biological tubes depart from ideal cylinders.

Pattern classes may be visually described without enough resolution for geodesic fitting.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.85

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Occurrence of the three thickening types is standard anatomy and can be checked in public micrographs of vessels and tracheae. Calling them geodesics is then almost a theorem, so the result does not separate the claim from ordinary anatomical description except where pitch is non-constant. Images suffice for a qualitative survey and not for a high-powered discrimination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On cylindrical vessels, tracheids and insect tracheae, classify wall thickenings as annular, longitudinal or helical and test whether helices have constant pitch. All three geodesic families, with constant-pitch helices, support the identification; spirals whose pitch varies along the cell refute the helical geodesic.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
On a cylinder, rings, generators and constant-pitch helices are the geodesics, so the label adds little once the pattern is named.

Quantitative pitch series are sparse compared with textbook illustrations of the three types.
